about: Hardware MIDI controllers that drive the JD-Xi Editor. Copy this file to ~/.jdxi_editor/midi_controllers.json (the editor does so on first start) and edit it there: an entry with the same id overrides the keys it gives of the built-in one, a new id adds a controller. 'control' is a FilterControl name: CUTOFF, RESONANCE, KEYFOLLOW, ENV_DEPTH, ENV_VELOCITY, ENV_ATTACK, ENV_DECAY, ENV_SUSTAIN, ENV_RELEASE, EFFECT1_LEVEL, EFFECT2_LEVEL, DELAY_LEVEL, REVERB_LEVEL. 'source' names the physical knob or fader for the MIDI Controller dialog. Port names are matched case-insensitively as substrings. Mappings learnt in the dialog are kept separately and take precedence. 'transport' lists transport buttons: action PLAY, PAUSE, STOP, RECORD, REWIND or FAST_FORWARD, sending a 'cc' (press 127, release 0) or a 'note', with optional 'channel' (0 = MIDI channel 1). Rewind and Fast Forward seek while held.

controllers.label: Arturia MiniLab 3
controllers.notes: Factory/User program, MIDI channel 1. Knobs 1-4 are the top row, 5-8 the bottom row. Which port carries the knobs depends on the device's mode, so every port is listened to; secondary ports only rank below the main one.

controllers.label: SINCO VMX8
controllers.notes: Translated from the MiniLab 3 map through ElMo's presets (elmo/midi/presets.py): MiniLab CC -> ElMo function -> ElMo VMX8 CC. CCs 32-39 are translations (zoom, rotation_x/y/z, translate_x/y, connolly_transparency, connolly_probe_radius); 40-43 are assigned, because MiniLab CCs 93, 16, 82 and 83 drive nothing in ElMo. ElMo's VMX8 preset is a placeholder, not measured: check these in the MIDI Monitor and fill in 'source'. The VMX8 repeats every message on its Private and Master ports, so only one port is opened. Transport: the buttons send notes 91-95 in the default mode and CCs 52-56 in CC mode; both are bound, so either mode works.
